messages:
zoe: Quick FYI  I'm opening a PR to tighten the model-card guidance for benchmark reporting, supported-variant metadata, and a short compatibility note for quant variants. Draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1598 :wave:

anil: Nice. Can you add a concise spec for the fields we expect in the card (e.g., tested_devices, seq_limit_per_variant, supported_quant, benchmark_notes)? Writers keep leaving out device info.

zoe: Yes. I propose adding a required small YAML block in the template and an example SDK + perf-harness snippet. Example YAML we'll include in the template: 
```
tested_devices: [a100,h100]
variants:
  - name: tempest13b-fp16
    seq_limit: 8192
    notes: "fp16 canonical"
  - name: tempest13b-int8
    seq_limit: 4096
    notes: "int8 uses chunked KV, lower seq ceiling"
benchmark_notes: "seq_len=1024 batch=1 warmup=50 iters=500; tokens_per_s is steady-state
"
```

carmen: That YAML looks good. Small ask: avoid very long inline tables in cards; include a 2-row illustrative example and link to the full model-catalog table for the canonical matrix.

fred: For cross-hardware comparisons, could we add a recommended normalization called "GFLOP-normalized throughput" so numbers are less misleading? Something like: norm_tps = measured_tps * (device_gflops / baseline_gflops). Call it heuristic and show a worked example.

zoe: Good idea. I'll add a short worked example: 
``
# example: measured 1200 tokens/s on a100 (312 TFLOPS perf), baseline = a100
norm_tps = 1200 * (312/312) = 1200
# if measured on v100 with 125 TFLOPS: norm_tps_to_a100 = 900 * (125/312) = 360 (heuristic)
``
and a note: "Do not use this for billing comparisons; it's for rough performance alignment only."

anil: Also call out variance when using hosted endpoints (5-15%) and instruct authors to mark numbers as "lab" vs "hosted".

carmen: For quant variants include a single-line compatibility note: "Quantized variants may change runtime memory patterns and sequence ceilings; verify seq_limit_per_variant before using long-context prompts." Link to model-catalog field anchor.

fred: SDK snippet please show fallback pattern and exact pip line, e.g.: 
```
# pip install redwood==2.1.0
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='tempest13b', variant='tempest13b-int8', fallback=['tempest13b-fp16'])
print(resp.text)
```

zoe: Adding that. Also scanning for stale perf links  I'll replace any link to /perf/benchmarks with https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness#readme and list changed files in the PR description.

anil: Reviewer plan: eng-ml for numbers + normalization sanity check, eng-runtime for variant naming/field names, docs for copyedit. Add a perf follow-up issue if we need canonical reruns.

docs-bot: Reminder: on PR open I will post the standard checklist (labels: docs, perf-needed if numbers changed, changenote). (automated)

zoe: One last small UI request: add a one-line reminder at the top of the model-card template: "Include baseline machine and test conditions (seq_len, batch, warmup iters)" so it's not missed. I'll add it to the PR.

carmen: LGTM. I'll do editorial pass once eng-ml signs off.

fred: pinging eng-ml now for a quick sanity pass.

zoe: thanks all  merging plan depends on eng-ml signoff; if timeline forces it we merge docs and file perf follow-up. last_message_ts=3523457025
